title: Integrating live AI services into games: how do you handle the costs and player expectations?
author: YouWitchApp
selftext:
I've developed a simple party game that uses AI image generation to turn player's selfies into witch characters based on what potions they drink throughout the game. I've enjoyed building the live AI service into the game and using Claude as a coding assistant to handle a lot of the third party integrations.

The main challenge has been balancing the cost of the AI services with the expectations of players. The service has a limited amount of free usage, and anything that goes over that would cost me money. I have set limits that I am willing to spend to cover people's games and added a system where players can buy their own credits if that runs out.  
  
I'm up front about using AI for the image manipulation, but still had people commenting on my videos calling me a scammer and a thief haha.

I wondered if anyone else here is using live AI services, and how they communicate the costs or use free credits, subscriptions or pay per use? Particularly an app that might have a one-time purchase, do you hope the user won't use more than the AI service costs?

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body: Don't even consider OTP, you have costs that needs to be covered, either BYOK which users will hate and most likely wont even figure out how to use or you sell credits or sub, there are too many variables, abuse and other factors that come with such services, I'd strongly advise you against going down this route without properly educating yourself first as you'd be talking about several thousands per mistake that can go into the 10s of thousands depending on how unlucky/lucky you are and there are many things you need to guard against. It's not rocket science, but when you don't know how to protect against abuse or bugs related to API calls to an AI provider you'll pay quiet a bit out of pocket.

replies.author: YouWitchApp
replies.body: Thanks! Yes I have a guard to stop abuse with a global rate limit. I was playing around with the idea of settling credits and a certain percentage of those sales contribute to a global credit pool

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body: Just generate 1000 images beforehand and match the image closest to the players picture at runtime. So you aren't actually paying any continuous charge

replies.author: YouWitchApp
replies.body: Hmm good idea for character portraits! In the case of my game the portrait is the end product so probably won't work for this game. Thanks though!

replies.author: Toastti
replies.body:
Then pre generate 10k photos with significant AI changes were it's hard to tell who the original person was. Then set those up in game to match the closest profile to the persons pic. 

If you have 10k images and a good matching system. (Along with a fake loader so people think generation is taking time) People will fully believe that you processed their unique profile pic. When in actually it's one of the 10k photos

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
figure out the pricing and bundle cheap api calls with self hosted image gen , vast ai cheap havent used them , went run pod not for gaming but to host llms like qwen to run queries for a few hours.

If there is demand the self host route is likely the best if not figure the pricing and charge with credits like anyone else.

Example 1.5 the price per gen and bundle it with other shit + pricing tiers (basic / advanced / pro) vibes. that is what all those selfie transformation apps did when they were hot, a bunch of gpus and comfyui variants
